proof.claim:
A package upgrade must reach every node that requires it, and "converged"
must mean observed, not dispatched.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The 2026-08-16 outage began as an ordinary package deploy.
The deploy reported success and the operator moved on; the rollout had not
converged, and the gap was found hours later through unrelated symptoms. The
suite had 68 scenarios at the time and not one of them exercised an upgrade,
which is the single most frequent mutation this platform performs.

THE DISTINCTION THIS PINS. A child workflow reporting SUCCEEDED is a dispatch
acknowledgement, not install proof
(reconcile.terminal_success_requires_observed_convergence). A rollout is
converged only when every required node proves the expected artifact is
installed AND running (rollout.convergence_requires_runtime_proof). Those two
are routinely conflated, and the conflation is invisible while the cluster is
healthy — it only shows up when one node is slow, partitioned, or missing the
blob, which is precisely when it matters.

Convergence identity is the build_id, not the version-only summary hash
(convergence.identity_is_build_id). A version that resolves to two build_ids
cannot converge deterministically, so this scenario also refuses to call a
rollout healthy while resolution is ambiguous.

This scenario observes the steady state rather than driving an upgrade
itself: it asserts that whatever the cluster currently believes it has
deployed is actually deployed, uniformly, everywhere. Run it after any
deploy — that is the check the pipeline used to skip.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
